text: Everything from the last three chapters exists to support one final piece: the chart of accounts, the classification scheme every transaction gets coded against. This lesson starts chapter five with how it's structured.

A chart of accounts is built from segments — ordered pieces like Company, Cost Center, Natural Account. Every transaction gets one value from each segment, and the full combination is called an account combination.

A chart of accounts structure defines the shape: how many segments, their order, their widths. A structure instance is an actual deployment of that shape, tied to specific value sets — two ledgers can share a structure but use different value sets.

How many segments and in what order is decided once, during design, and should not be revisited casually. Too few and you can't report what you need; too many and every screen and report gets harder to use.
Once a structure is defined, it gets frozen, then deployed, before any ledger can use it. Next up, lesson twenty-one: segment labels — balancing, cost center, and natural account.
